newsitem.title: JAPAN: Burma crude oil, diesel payments delayed - Mitsui.
newsitem.headline: Burma crude oil, diesel payments delayed - Mitsui.

text.p: Mitsui & Co Ltd said on Friday that Burma was behind in some of its payments of crude oil and diesel fuel sold under annual term contracts, due to operational reasons.
"Burma is slightly behind in some of its payments," a Mitsui spokesman said. "We believe this is due to delays in operational matters such as issuing letters of credit."
Mitsui has fulfilled all obligations of the term contract which expired September 7, including cargo loadings, he said.
Mitsui would not disclose the volume of crude oil and diesel fuel supplied to Burma under the contract.
Mitsui was awarded the annual contract through a tender, the spokesman said.
Petrol and diesel prices have soared on the Burmese black market on panic buying triggered by rumours in Rangoon that a foreign company had recently stopped supplying crude to Burma.
On September 14, democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi told supporters the military government owed $31 million to a foreign company supplying essential chemicals, which is why supplies stopped.

Mitsui said the delay in payments would not hinder the trading houses' future participation in tenders issued by Burma. "We do not know when Burma will issue its next tender but we plan to take part, depending on the terms," the spokesman said.
